title: OKF index progressive disclosure: compact index -> drill into relevant articles
priority_note: The 'load the index, then drill only into relevant docs' half of the OKF pattern — reduces over-retrieval. Reuses knowledge_index + hubs + OKF. Depends on the curated rule (31.1).

background.reference: GitHub issues #305/#306 ('OKF index files for progressive disclosure'); hub 820602df; reuses Loopctl.Knowledge index/hub + okf.ex + the knowledge_index controller.
background.includes: Rather than over-retrieving chunks, an agent should load a compact index (hubs / OKF index files) and drill into only the relevant curated articles. loopctl already has knowledge_index (category view), hubs, and OKF export; this story composes them into a progressive-disclosure entrypoint.

story.i_want_to: fetch a compact index/hub for a topic and then drill into only the relevant curated articles
story.so_that: I navigate by index (few tokens) instead of over-retrieving many fuzzy chunks

rationale: Karpathy's 'navigate by index' rule and the OKF index-file pattern both say the model should read a compact index and follow the few relevant pages, not scan the corpus. Exposing loopctl's existing hub/index/OKF layer as a progressive-disclosure path is the token-efficiency half of the hybrid interface and complements the resolver (31.2).

acceptance_criteria.description: A progressive-disclosure entrypoint returns, for a topic/query, a COMPACT index (hub + linked curated article stubs: id, title, category, one-line summary) rather than full bodies — reusing knowledge_index / hub structure / OKF index files, tenant-scoped.
A drill step fetches the full body of a chosen indexed article by id (scope-enforced), so the agent loads only what the index pointed at.
The index prefers curated sources (US-31.1) and reflects OKF index files where present (reuse knowledge_okf_export/okf.ex index representation); it does not dump the whole corpus.
Tenant isolation: the index and drill only expose the caller tenant's articles.

test_cases.name: index returns compact stubs then drill returns the body
preconditions: a hub linking several curated articles
steps: fetch the progressive index for the hub's topic
expected_results: index returns stubs (id/title/summary, not full bodies); drill returns the full article body; token-compact

technical_notes: Reuse the knowledge_index controller/context + hub link structure + okf.ex index representation; do not build a new index store.
Compact stub = id, title, category, short summary/first line — NOT the full body (that is the drill step).
Tenant scoping via the existing knowledge scope mechanism.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 with a hub + linked articles.
